The vendor entity behind all three is OpenAI.

privacy.ai_training_note: Training posture differs by product tier. For the API platform (which hosts the Whisper transcription/translation endpoints) and ChatGPT Team/Enterprise/Edu, OpenAI processes Customer Data only per customer instructions under the executed DPA, and multiple independent secondary sources report that API and business data is not used to train models unless the customer explicitly opts in. Free and Plus ChatGPT (which also surface Whisper-based voice features) have a different, less protective default and historically may use conversations to improve models unless the user opts out in settings; the 'no training' claim does not extend to that tier. The open-source Whisper model runs entirely on the user's own infrastructure, so no OpenAI training-on-your-data question applies. Third-party reporting (Basil AI, Nov 2025) alleges the Whisper API's 'zero data retention' marketing claim is inconsistent with an actual retention window of about 30 days for abuse monitoring; OpenAI's own current wording on this point is not independently confirmed.
privacy.data_region: Self-hosted open-source Whisper: fully user-controlled, no data leaves user infrastructure. API/ChatGPT: processed on OpenAI's cloud infrastructure; OpenAI Ireland Ltd. is the contracting/processing entity for EEA and Swiss data with Standard Contractual Clauses governing onward transfers; no Whisper-specific regional data-residency option was found in public documentation.

security.name: Independent audit coverage
security.value: SOC 2 Type II and SOC 3 reports cover OpenAI's API platform, ChatGPT Enterprise, and ChatGPT Edu; free/Plus ChatGPT is explicitly excluded per independent secondary reporting (not itemized on the trust portal overview itself).

security.name: ISMS certification
security.value: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Information Security Management System certified for OpenAI's API, ChatGPT Enterprise, and ChatGPT Edu services, extended with ISO 27017 (cloud), ISO 27018 (PII in cloud), and ISO 27701 (privacy) control sets.

security.name: Sub-processor transparency
security.value: A public sub-processor list is maintained and customers are notified of additions with a 30-day objection window under the DPA.

security.name: Breach notification
security.value: DPA commits OpenAI to notify customers "without undue delay after becoming aware of any Personal Data Breach."

security.name: Encryption specifics
security.value: The DPA commits generically to "reasonable and appropriate organizational and technical security measures... as set forth in the Agreement" without stating a specific algorithm. Specific claims seen in secondary write-ups (e.g., AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit) are not confirmed on a vendor-owned page.

security.name: Self-hosted model (open-source Whisper)
security.value: No OpenAI-side security controls apply because no data is transmitted to OpenAI; the security posture of a self-hosted deployment is entirely the responsibility of the organization running it.

products.name: Whisper (open-source model)
products.data_scope: None sent to OpenAI; runs entirely on the user's own hardware/infrastructure via local inference.
products.notes: MIT-licensed code and weights, installable via `pip install openai-whisper` / GitHub. No OpenAI certification applies or is needed since no OpenAI infrastructure is involved; security is fully the deploying organization's responsibility.

products.name: Whisper API (hosted transcription/translation endpoints)
products.data_scope: Audio input and transcription/translation output are sent to and processed on OpenAI's servers; per secondary reporting, retained for up to approximately 30 days for abuse and misuse monitoring, then deleted; not used for model training by default.
products.notes: Part of the general-availability OpenAI API platform. Trust-portal certifications (SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001/27017/27018/27701) describe coverage of 'OpenAI's API' as a whole; Whisper's specific endpoints are not separately named on the public trust-portal page, so coverage is a reasonable inference rather than an explicit vendor statement.

products.name: ChatGPT voice features (Whisper-family models embedded in ChatGPT)
products.data_scope: Voice input is processed as part of the broader ChatGPT conversation; data handling and training defaults differ sharply by plan.
products.notes: ChatGPT Team, Enterprise, and Edu are covered by SOC 2/ISO certifications and are not used for model training by default. Free and Plus ChatGPT are not covered by SOC 2 per independent reporting, and conversation data (including voice) may be used to improve models unless the user opts out in settings.

compare.pricing_model: Open-source model: free (self-hosted compute cost only). API: pay-per-use, priced per minute of audio processed. ChatGPT voice: bundled within Free/Plus/Team/Enterprise/Edu subscription tiers.
compare.data_residency: Self-hosted variant: fully user-controlled. API/ChatGPT variant: OpenAI cloud infrastructure with OpenAI Ireland Ltd. as EEA/Swiss contracting entity and SCC-based international transfer safeguards; no Whisper-specific regional residency option documented.
top_certs: SOC 2 Type II (API / ChatGPT Enterprise / Edu)

flags: Product-scope inference: OpenAI's trust portal lists certifications for 'OpenAI's API, ChatGPT Enterprise, and ChatGPT Edu' but never names 'Whisper', 'audio', or 'transcription' explicitly; treating the Whisper API as covered is a reasonable but unconfirmed inference.
Free and Plus ChatGPT (which also surface Whisper-based voice input) are explicitly excluded from SOC 2 coverage per independent reporting; SOC 2 does not apply to those tiers.

Third-party reporting (Basil AI, Nov 2025) alleges the Whisper API is marketed with a 'zero data retention' claim while actually retaining audio for up to approximately 30 days for abuse monitoring. OpenAI's own current wording on this point is not independently confirmed on its policy pages.

HIPAA is not listed as a certification or badge on OpenAI's own trust portal. Secondary sources describe a case-by-case Business Associate Agreement (BAA) for API and healthcare customers rather than a certification; where noted, it should be labeled 'BAA available on request, case-by-case.'
Not to be confused with the unrelated product 'WhisperAI' (whisperai.com), a separate company and domain.

FedRAMP 20x and TX-RAMP badges likely scope to OpenAI's government-specific offerings, not the general-availability Whisper API; the public trust-portal overview does not break out per-product scope for these two.
